quests.name: Abyssal Current
quests.shortDescription: A bioluminescent deep-sea simulator that teaches CSS @keyframes, animation timing, and easing functions through environmental survival.
quests.longDescription:
## Abyssal Current

Pilot a glowing submersible through pitch-black ocean trenches where the only light comes from CSS animations you construct. Drag keyframe "buoys" onto a timeline reel to build `@keyframes` while your sub's bioluminescence animates live.

### Features

- Real-time CSS injection engine updates the game world instantly as you manipulate the timeline.
- Physical drag-and-drop keyframe buoys representing specific CSS transformations, scale, and hue rotations.
- Live easing visualizer that demonstrates the mathematical difference between linear and ease-in-out functions using particle currents.
- Ghost UI hints and survival mechanics: An oxygen/pressure gauge that steadily drains, forcing players to quickly grasp and apply the correct animation sequence to clear the sector.
- High-fidelity, procedurally animated SVG deep-sea creatures (Jellyfish, Anglerfish, Octopus, Seahorse) that sync with your animation states.
- Fully responsive layout utilizing raw Vanilla JS and CSS variables, with absolutely zero external frameworks.

quests.name: Accessibility Audit Quest
quests.shortDescription: Find and fix accessibility (a11y) issues in broken HTML snippets.
quests.longDescription:
## Accessibility Audit Quest

An interactive quest where you play as an accessibility auditor. Find and fix common a11y issues in broken HTML snippets to make the web more inclusive.

### Features

- Multiple levels with broken HTML snippets.
- Learn to identify and fix issues like missing alt text, improper heading structure, and low contrast.
- Real-time feedback and explanations.
- Progress saved locally.

quests.name: Branch Navigator
quests.shortDescription: A lightweight Git quest (Easy) to learn checkout basics by navigating a commit graph with `git log`, `git branch`, and `git checkout`.
quests.longDescription:
## Branch Navigator

Navigate a commit graph like a time traveler. Start from the newest commit and use Git commands in an interactive terminal to reach specific commits and branches.

### Features

- 3 easy levels
- Learn `git log`, `git branch`, and `git checkout`
- Visual commit graph with HEAD and branch labels
- Goal-based terminal completion + progress saved locally
- Fully offline, single-file quest

quests.name: Closure Escape Room

quests.longDescription:
## Closure Escape Room

An escape-room themed JavaScript quest where every locked door is opened by solving a closure puzzle. Learn how closures capture variables, understand lexical scope, debug common mistakes, and master private state through interactive challenges.

### Features

- 10 progressively challenging escape rooms
- Learn closures, lexical scope, callbacks, private variables, and data encapsulation
- Interactive puzzles with real-time feedback and explanations
- Hint system for difficult challenges
- Progress saved locally using localStorage
- Responsive and keyboard accessible
- Works completely offline

quests.name: Flexbox Frenzy: The Alignment Heist
quests.shortDescription: A heist caper where every vault lock is a Flexbox puzzle — write real CSS to slide gold bars onto their targets, judged live by the browser's own layout engine, scored on how few properties you use.
quests.longDescription:
## Flexbox Frenzy: The Alignment Heist

Crack vaults by solving Flexbox puzzles. Ghostly target outlines show where the gold bars must end up; you write real CSS on the container to slide them into position, and when every bar overlaps its target the vault clicks open. The honest twist: your CSS is applied to actual DOM elements and measured live with `getBoundingClientRect`, so the browser's own layout engine decides whether you cracked the lock. CSS isn't simulated here — it is the render engine and the judge.

### Features

- Real Flexbox layout as the game engine: properties are applied to live containers and gold bars animate to wherever the browser actually lays them out; a `getBoundingClientRect` overlap check seats each bar. Nothing is hand-authored.
- Finesse scoring (golf for CSS): validity is only the entry fee — your score is how few properties you used, rewarding shorthands like `place-content: center` over separate `justify-content` and `align-items`.
- Procedural vaults with verified solutions: every layout is generated from a known-achievable property set, so par is real, difficulty scales, and no two heists repeat.
- Five escalating floors: main-axis (`justify-content`), cross-axis (`align-items`), `flex-direction` flips that make the same properties behave differently, `gap`/`flex-grow`/`align-self`, and a timed vault-crack boss where finesse buys time.
- Teaches the single most confusing thing about Flexbox — which axis a property acts on — by flipping `flex-direction` mid-game and letting you watch your assumptions break and correct.
- Pure visual payoff: gold bars sliding into laser-gridded vaults, Canvas particle bursts on a vault opening, synthetic Web Audio SFX, and a heist-scorecard summary, built in pure vanilla JavaScript with full `prefers-reduced-motion` support and zero external frameworks.

quests.name: Memory Heap Detective
quests.shortDescription: Interactive memory profiling and garbage collection diagnostic simulator for learning JavaScript memory management and leak prevention.
quests.longDescription:
## Memory Heap Detective

An interactive memory profiling and garbage collection diagnostic simulator that teaches memory management, heap snapshot analysis, and memory leak prevention in JavaScript.

### Features

- Interactive Heap Snapshot Visualizer: Real-time visual memory graph displaying GC Roots, Detached DOM Trees, Retainer Chains, and Allocation Timelines
- Memory Leak Diagnostic Challenges: Level-based scenarios covering dangling event listeners, detached DOM nodes, uncleared timers, and circular reference traps
- Real-Time Garbage Collector Simulator: Manual 'Trigger GC' sweep button that reclaims freed memory and updates heap allocation charts
- Web Audio Synthesizer SFX: Audio feedback for GC sweeps, memory alarms, and level completion fanfares
- Built-In Memory Profiling Manual: Cheatsheet covering V8 Garbage Collection mechanics (Mark-and-Sweep, Generational GC)

quests.name: Regex CSS Golf
quests.shortDescription: Master CSS selectors through interactive golf-style challenges by writing the shortest valid selector to match target elements.
quests.longDescription:
## Regex CSS Golf

Sharpen your CSS selector skills with golf-style puzzles. Write the shortest valid CSS selector that matches only the highlighted target elements while avoiding all others. Progress through increasingly challenging levels covering combinators, pseudo-classes, attribute selectors, and structural selectors.

### Features

- Progressive CSS selector challenges
- Real-time validation and feedback
- Golf scoring based on selector length
- Learn combinators, attribute selectors, and pseudo-classes
- Local progress saving using localStorage
- Fully offline, single-file quest

quests.name: Strata: The Lost Commits
quests.shortDescription: A field excavation of version history; an interactive Git rebase simulator that turns commit history cleanup into an archaeological dig.
quests.longDescription:
## Strata: The Lost Commits

Four sites, each hiding a scattered commit history beneath the soil. You are an archivist tasked with cleaning up messy git history before it merges into the main branch. Every digging tool corresponds to a real `git rebase -i` command.

### Features

- Four distinct excavation sites, each with unique historical stratigraphy (commit history)
- Authentic Git mechanics mapped to archaeological tools: Pick (keep), Reword (rename), Squash (bond), Fixup (patch), and Drop (shatter)
- Preservation meter that challenges you to perform the most accurate rebase possible
- Interactive Finds Table to reorder and finalize your commit history
- In-game Archivist's Guide explaining the Git theory behind each dig
- Analog-archaeological aesthetic with hand-drawn SVG elements and custom fonts
- Progress saved locally via localStorage
- Fully self-contained single HTML file with no external dependencies

quests.name: The Merge Conflict from Hell
quests.shortDescription: A horror-themed terminal escape room that teaches real Git commands — staging, detached HEAD, conflict resolution, and force pushing — under a draining sanity meter.
quests.longDescription:
## The Merge Conflict from Hell

Midnight. The server room door locks itself. The spirit of a corrupted Senior Developer — The Detached HEAD — has trapped your soul in a dirty working tree. Escape by typing real Git commands into a possessed Bash terminal across four corrupted branches, before your sanity hits zero and you are hard-deleted from `main`.

### Features

- Fully interactive faux Bash terminal that parses and evaluates real Git commands: `git add`, `commit`, `checkout -b`, `rebase`, and `push --force`, with honest `git status` output as the core teaching mechanic.
- Four escalating levels: selective staging in a haunted component tree, a maze where phantom commits detach HEAD and invert your controls, a three-hunk merge conflict resolver, and a 60-second rapid-fire command finale.
- 100% synthetic Web Audio horror soundscape — looping server-room hum, jumpscare screeches, and a heartbeat whose tempo tracks your remaining sanity. No audio files.
- Reactive dread systems: sanity meter, screen shake, CRT scanlines, canvas static bursts, random scheduled jumpscares, and whole-page micro-glitches that intensify as you fail.
- Digital blood splatter victory sequence via canvas-confetti, plus command history recall, per-level hints, and Git-flavoured easter eggs (`git blame`, `sudo`, `git reset --hard`).
- Graceful degradation with library fallbacks and full `prefers-reduced-motion` support that kills the theatrics but keeps the game playable.

quests.name: The Reconciler
quests.shortDescription: A Victorian manor horror where the house is a live React component tree — fix one-way props, state re-renders, effect cleanup, and reconciliation keys floor by floor while a living fiber-tree diagram reflects it all in real time.
quests.longDescription:
## The Reconciler

2 AM. A haunted house app's deploy goes wrong, and you get pulled inside it. The foyer is `<App>`; every door leads to a child. Something called The Reconciler lives in the walls — the process deciding what changes and what stays when the tree re-renders — and it has been running wrong for years. Duplicated furniture, doors that forget their state, rooms rebuilding into oblivion. Escape by fixing the house's React, floor by floor.

### Features

- Living fiber-tree diagram rendered alongside the manor cross-section, reflecting the actual component tree the player is standing inside — nodes pulse on render, split on new children, rewire on reorder.
- Four floors teaching distinct React concepts: one-way prop flow (carrying a lantern down through nested rooms without setting it down), state updates triggering re-renders (an unguarded render loop that rebuilds a room faster and faster), `useEffect` dependencies and cleanup (a stale-closure ghost and a torn-down room whose effect never cleaned up), and keys in reconciliation (a shuffling portrait hallway that swaps identities without stable keys).
- Canvas-based diff-spark particle system marking the moment the Reconciler decides to patch versus replace a node.
- Framer Motion room-to-room morphs so floors dissolve into each other rather than cutting between screens.
- Layered parallax SVG art for the manor interior — candlelight, dust motes, warping wallpaper that glitches when the Reconciler misbehaves.
- Distinct horror palette: aged brass and candlelight amber against near-black oak, with a single sickly violet reserved for The Reconciler itself, plus full `prefers-reduced-motion` support.

quests.name: XSS Defender
quests.shortDescription: Interactive web security quest game teaching Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) prevention, HTML sanitization, and Content Security Policy (CSP) headers.
quests.longDescription:
## XSS Defender

An interactive web security quest game that teaches Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) prevention, HTML sanitizer policies (DOMPurify / HTML Sanitizer API), and Content Security Policy (CSP) directive configurations.

### Features

- Interactive XSS Attack Simulator: Live rendering of attack payloads in an isolated preview sandbox
- Progressive Security Levels: Level-based scenarios covering Reflected XSS entity encoding, DOM sanitization policies, CSP headers, and event handler attribute injections
- Real-Time Vulnerability Analyzer: Live feedback indicating whether script execution was blocked or succeeded
- Web Audio Synthesizer SFX: Audio feedback for firewall alerts, sanitization shield activations, and level completion fanfares
- Built-In Web Security Manual: Cheatsheet covering XSS prevention guidelines and CSP directive syntax
